headline: Reuters says AI leaders are split on how fast to build: Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX chiefs want a coordinated slowdown, while Meta's Mark Zuckerberg and Nvidia's Jensen Huang push back.
score_reason: A useful roundup of positions, but it collects statements made over several days rather than reporting one new event. Lowered from 6.
importance_line: It shows readers where the people building AI disagree on pace and rules, but it is a summary of stated views, and several backers of a slowdown also sell AI.
summary: Reuters reports in a factbox of 14 Oct 2026 that Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, argued in an essay for pacing the frontier of AI development, OpenAI chief Sam Altman and SpaceX chief Elon Musk backed him, and OpenAI said it will adopt independent evaluators with employee-like access. Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive of Meta, rejected a slowdown and put safety on each lab, and Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, told CBS News there is "0% chance" AI ends the world; BlackRock chief Larry Fink warned that a data centre moratorium would cause a recession.
notes: Read the Reuters factbox as carried by the Lufkin Daily News (copy site); source credited to Reuters. Url is the copy page, as the original Reuters link was not available. Score lowered 6 to 5: compiles earlier statements.
